evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Arden: 'before we proceed with the estimate, I need to ask you questions regarding the move that might take around ten to fifteen minutes would that be fine?' — framing present but rushed past without waiting for explicit 'yes' confirmation on the time commitment and quote promise before launching into the agenda question.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Arden: 'other than the price by the way Jennifer also, what are your biggest concerns about this move and what do you want answers to within the calls?' — asked before any logistics probing, customer raised damaged items from prior move and date flexibility concerns.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Arden: 'were they able to, were they able to refund or at least pay you or do repairs for what was damaged' (follow-up on damage concern). Customer responds about $75 payment. Arden follows up again: 'I understand' then pivots to assurance about Einstein's coverage — genuine two-layer dig into the damage anxiety, then address it head-on with the No Worries coverage pitch.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: Not present — Arden acknowledges concerns ('I understand') but never reflects back 'so what I'm hearing is X, Y, and Z. Did I get all of it?' No summary confirmation of all stated concerns.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Property type (one bedroom apartment), floor (third floor with staircase access), unit number (2306), parking (can park in front), walking distance (8 feet to staircase, 8–10 feet to apartment), storage unit destination (10x10, first floor, indoor drive-up with two sliding doors, 5 feet from door to corner), items requiring care (valuable glass in boxes, one TV under 65 inches, 30 book boxes max). All seven logistics categories covered.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Arden: 'Since how many maximum number of boxes do you think are we going to move for you guest' — Customer: 'I have book boxes which are small but heavy but there's just books, I'm gonna guess I have no more than thirty.' Arden: 'Thirty. Okay, it's okay. Maximum is thirty.'
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Not offered — Arden never asked if Einstein should pack items into boxes.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Arden: 'typically a one bedroom apartment usually takes two movers between two and a half to three and a half hours' (typical range), then personalized: 'in your case since we're going to be moving you from the third floor...into a first floor storage unit...I'm estimating them will take only around two and a half to three hours and fifteen minutes. So, it's good to budget an overall of $555 to $699 for the move.' Range provided and personalized to staircase load/first-floor unload.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Arden: 'we charge an hourly rate of $192 per hour for two movers...Everything is already included in that hourly rate, gas trucks, taxes, insurance all the wraps, the pads and bans...The only thing outside that hour rate is a one time transportation fee of $75...no hidden fees...no credit card fees, no terrible fees and no disassemble or reassembly fees.' Also: 'it's a two and a half hour minimum. Once we go over the minimum the time will be prorated in fifteen minutes. Increment.' Full transparency and commitment framing present.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked — Arden moves directly from pricing explanation to booking options ('now your choice, ma'am, we either reschedule you for the thirtieth or rescheduled you for the 6th of October') without asking 'Does that feel fair?' or pausing for customer reaction.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Arden: 'we have an on time guarantee. If the movers arrive late, you start to get discount on your final bill. The later day arrive the bigger discount will be okay.' Also: 'if the movers arrive late, you start to get discount, the later they arrive, the bigger, the discount will be okay.' Discount terms stated directly — full delivery.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Arden: 'included in your hourly rate that you're gonna be paying...a free evaluation coverage that provides up to $2,000 per move...zero deductible. It's either going to be repaired, replaced, reimbursed and that's gonna be handled in three to five business days.' Later: 'we're gonna give you up to $2,000 per move to file a claim for repair replacement or reimbursement for any accidental damage...Giving you a peace of mind that we'll be able to cover your high value items.' $2,000 coverage, no deductible, built into hourly rate fully stated.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: Arden does not ask 'Does that put those to rest?' or similar closing check on the Two Promises. Moves directly to date selection after the coverage explanation.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Not asked — Arden jumps from booking confirmation directly to sending the email confirmation without asking 'What's still concerning you about this move?' or any version of a genuine final-concerns check.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: Not asked — Arden never asks 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?'
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Never asked — Arden never says 'Would you like our help with your move?' or any recognizable explicit ask. Instead moves to date selection ('your choice, ma'am, we either reschedule you for the thirtieth or rescheduled you for the 6th') as a closed choice, treating the booking as already decided.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: Arden: 'we don't require any deposit or upfront payment to book or do a booking a reservation with us.' Rate lock / no-deposit explicitly stated.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Arden confirms: date (6th of October, Tuesday), time window (8:30 to 9:00 a.m.), and sends confirmation email with details. However, phone number and crew size NOT confirmed in the call. Customer does not explicitly confirm addresses (pickup and storage destination are mentioned but not a final address check-in). No notes left for crew about customer's damage anxiety or prior bad experience. Partial confirmation.

top_strength: Arden performed excellent two-layer probing on the customer's damage anxiety from her prior move, surfacing the real pain point and then directly addressing it with Einstein's No Worries coverage—turning a major objection into a credibility differentiator.
coaching_note: Never skip the 'Does that feel fair?' pause and final-concerns check before booking; move directly to date selection without an explicit ask or genuine silence kill closes the customer prematurely and leaves objections buried until after the sale.
